title: Object Declarations and Object Expressions

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Object Declarations and Object Expressions** as part of **Classes, Objects, and Object-Oriented Fundamentals**. An `object` declaration creates a named singleton; use it for a single shared instance, not as a replacement for every dependency. Use the subtopics—Singleton Object Declarations, Anonymous Object Expressions, Common Use Cases—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: These concepts help you model domain rules and reusable APIs. Good boundaries reduce accidental mutation, unsafe casts, and code that is difficult to extend.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: An `object` declaration creates a named singleton; use it for a single shared instance, not as a replacement for every dependency.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about it
content_blocks.text: Start with singleton object declarations. Then compare it with anonymous object expressions. Identify the input, state, dependency, or branch that determines the result. The snippet is a static reference for CodeLeaf and is not executed in the lesson page.

items.title: Singleton Object Declarations
items.text: Singleton Object Declarations should support a clear object invariant: make valid states easy to represent, restrict mutation to the intended API, and keep initialization and dependencies explicit.

items.title: Anonymous Object Expressions
items.text: Anonymous Object Expressions should support a clear object invariant: make valid states easy to represent, restrict mutation to the intended API, and keep initialization and dependencies explicit.

fun main() = println(AppInfo.name)
